title: Annual Report - 2024: Supervision and Regulation
summary: This chapter of the Federal Reserve's 2024 Annual Report describes the Fed's supervisory and regulatory framework for banking organizations as of year-end 2024, categorizing institutions by portfolio type and providing aggregate asset data across bank holding companies, state member banks, savings and loan holding companies, and financial market utilities.
key_points: The Fed categorizes supervised institutions into portfolios: CBOs (under $10B assets), RBOs ($10-100B), LFBOs ($100B+ and foreign banks), and LISCC (8 U.S. G-SIBs)
As of December 31, 2024, 3,747 U.S. bank holding companies controlled approximately 95% of all insured commercial bank assets
The LISCC portfolio includes 8 U.S. G-SIBs with $15.2 trillion in total assets and 4 state member banks within those organizations
State member banks numbered 1,402, operating 47,434 branches representing 35% of all U.S. commercial banks and 70% of all commercial banking offices
497 domestic BHCs and 46 foreign banking organizations held Financial Holding Company (FHC) status as of year-end 2025
Five supervised insurance organizations (SLHCs) with approximately $450 billion in total assets were supervised by the Fed at year-end 2024
FSOC designated eight Financial Market Utilities (FMUs) as systemically important under Title VIII of Dodd-Frank in July 2012
why_it_matters: This document provides baseline institutional knowledge about the Fed's supervisory taxonomy and banking sector composition as of year-end 2024. For market structure analysis, the FMU designation information is the most directly relevant element, though the discussion is brief and non-actionable.
market_structure_context: The source discusses Financial Market Utilities (FMUs) that manage multilateral systems for transferring, clearing, and settling payments and securities. The Fed supervises FMUs chartered as member banks or Edge Act corporations, with FSOC having designated eight FMUs as systemically important under Dodd-Frank Title VIII in July 2012 (no operational details or updates provided). This is the only market infrastructure element in an otherwise supervisory/regulatory overview.
important_numbers: 47,434 branches (35% of commercial banks, 70% of offices)
8 systemically important FMUs designated by FSOC
